newsitem.title: USA: Ahmanson wins backing for four proposals.
newsitem.headline: Ahmanson wins backing for four proposals.

text.p: Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS), a group that advises institutional shareholders on how to vote in proxy and consent solications, Wednesday backed four of the five proposals on which it seeks consents from shareholders of Great Western Financial Corp.

According to a copy of the recommendations, ISS endorsed Ahmanson's proposal that shareholders approve a non-binding resolution requiring the Great Western board to particpate in merger discussions with Ahmanson.

ISS said it was not favoring Ahmanson's bid for Great Western, nor is it favoring rival bidder Washington Mutual Inc. Wall Street considers Ahmanson's bid to be hostile and Great Western has agreed to a merger with Seattle-based Washington Mutual. Both Ahmanson and Great Western are based in Southern California.

ISS backed an Ahmanson proposal seeking shareholder approval of an amendment to the Great Western bylaws that would require the company to hold its annual meeting on the fourth Tuesday in April, or on a date within 14 days of that date.

ISS also backed an Ahmanson proposal that would amend the Great Western bylaws to provide that the holders of a majority of stock having voting power, whether in person or by proxy, shall make up a quorum. ISS said that, as a matter of policy, it believes that, when a quorum is present or represented by proxy, management should not adjourn meetings until all business has been done.

ISS said it backed an Ahmanson proposal seeking shareholder approval of an amendment to the Great Western bylaws that would prohibit repeal of amendments adopted in the solicitation without an affirmative majority vote.

ISS advised against voting for an Ahmanson propoosal seeking approval of a non-binding resolution that would urge the board not to grant break-up fees, or other "lock-up" agreements worth more than $100 million without shareholder approval.
ISS said that, without the termination fee in the deal with Washington Mutual, worth as much as $195 million, Great Western may not have been able to convince Washington Mutual to start negotiations.
Peter Gleason, an ISS analyst who prepared the report, was not immediately available for further comment.
